description: Amplitude product-analytics SDK. Two generations: legacy v1 (artifact com.amplitude:android-sdk, package com.amplitude.api, static facade Amplitude + instance AmplitudeClient) and current v2 (artifact com.amplitude:analytics-android, packages com.amplitude.android + com.amplitude.core, class Amplitude). CRITICAL: both the AmplitudeClient (v1) and the Amplitude (v2) instances are FLUENT builders — nearly every method (initialize, setUserId, setDeviceId, track, identify, logRevenue, setGroup, groupIdentify, enableForegroundTracking, useAdvertisingIdForDeviceId, ...) returns the client itself for chaining. Null-returning any of them would break the app's call chain and NPE, so they are NOT stubbed here. Only genuinely void, fire-and-forget calls are stubbed: the v1 static facade (com.amplitude.api.Amplitude.*, all static void), the v1 AmplitudeClient void reporting calls (logEvent/logEventSync/logRevenue/logRevenueV2/setUserProperties/identify/setGroup/groupIdentify/uploadEvents), and the v2 flush() (the only void method on the v2 client). getUserId/getDeviceId (String) are protected. Amplitude uploads over OkHttp on worker threads with no manifest service/receiver, so there are no manifest components to disable. Verified against analytics-core 1.33.0 (v2) and android-sdk 3.35.1 (v1); no local decode available.

methods.name: flush
methods.note: v2 flush — the ONLY void method on the v2 client. All v2 track/identify/setUserId/setDeviceId/setGroup/groupIdentify/revenue/logRevenue calls return com.amplitude.core.Amplitude (fluent) and are protected, not stubbed

methods.name: flush
methods.note: v2 Android subclass flush (inherited void); harmless duplicate of core flush for apps typed against the concrete class

protected_patterns.reason: v1 com.amplitude.api.Amplitude.getInstance() returns the shared AmplitudeClient the app then chains on; null would NPE the whole init chain
String getter (v1 AmplitudeClient / v2 Amplitude); the app may read and dereference it, so it is left working
String getter (v1 facade + instance, v2 Amplitude); returns the resolved device id the app may read; null could NPE callers. Left working

v2 track(...) is FLUENT: returns com.amplitude.core.Amplitude (this) for chaining. Null-returning it would break call chains and NPE, so it is deliberately NOT in entry_points. (v1 AmplitudeClient.setUserId / .setDeviceId / .initialize are fluent for the same reason and are simply left out of entry_points; only the v1 static facade's void setUserId/initialize are stubbed. These names are not protected here because that would also un-stub the safe void facade versions — registry-scan.py excludes protected method names globally.)
v1 AmplitudeClient.setDeviceId and v2 Amplitude.setDeviceId are FLUENT (return the client). setDeviceId is never a stub target, so protecting the name is safe and documents the fluent risk
